title: Introduction to qrme: Quantile Regression with Measurement Error
text: qrme package estimates quantile regression (QR) models dependent variable measured error. Classical QR applied noisy outcomes produces biased estimates conditional quantile function true (latent) outcome. qrme() corrects bias via pseudo-EM algorithm alternates E-step — drawing latent true outcomes given observed noisy outcome current QR parameters, using Metropolis–Hastings MCMC; M-step — re-fitting quantile regressions augmented data. case outcome continuous treatment variable measured error, see vignette("tsme-application"), describes tsme().

title: Introduction to qrme: Quantile Regression with Measurement Error
text: use location-scale DGP true outcome Y*Y^* depends uniform covariate XX: Y*=β0(U)+β1(U)X,U∼Uniform(0,1), Y^* = \beta_0(U) + \beta_1(U)\,X, \quad U \sim \text{Uniform}(0,1), β0(u)=1+3u−u2,β1(u)=eu. \beta_0(u) = 1 + 3u - u^2, \qquad \beta_1(u) = e^u. observed outcome Y=Y*+VY = Y^* + V, V∼N(0,σV2)V \sim N(0, \sigma_V^2) σV=0.5\sigma_V = 0.5.
code: library(qrme) library(quantreg) #> Loading required package: SparseM  n   <- 400 tau <- seq(0.10, 0.90, by = 0.10)  # true coefficient functions b0 <- function(u) 1 + 3 * u - u^2 b1 <- function(u) exp(u)  X     <- runif(n) U     <- runif(n) Ystar <- b0(U) + b1(U) * X          # latent outcome V     <- rnorm(n, sd = 0.5)         # measurement error Y     <- Ystar + V                   # observed (noisy) outcome  dd <- data.frame(Y = Y, Ystar = Ystar, X = X)

title: Introduction to qrme: Quantile Regression with Measurement Error
text: QR coefficient matrix lives fit_me$bet. Rows correspond tau values; columns regression coefficients (intercept first). Use betfun() get smooth interpolating function unit interval, useful plotting full quantile process:  -corrected estimates track truth substantially better naive estimates, especially extreme quantiles.
code: # intercept and slope at each quantile colnames(fit_me$bet) <- c("intercept", "slope_X") round(fit_me$bet, 3) #>          intercept slope_X #> tau= 0.1     1.556   1.516 #> tau= 0.2     1.647   1.575 #> tau= 0.3     1.814   1.564 #> tau= 0.4     2.017   1.617 #> tau= 0.5     2.206   1.756 #> tau= 0.6     2.319   1.956 #> tau= 0.7     2.395   2.226 #> tau= 0.8     2.454   2.437 #> tau= 0.9     2.519   2.544 bf    <- betfun(fit_me$bet, tau) tau_g <- seq(0.10, 0.90, length.out = 200)  # betfun returns a function over scalar tau; sapply to vectorise slope_me    <- sapply(tau_g, function(u) bf(u)[2]) bf_noisy    <- betfun(t(coef(fit_noisy)), tau) slope_noisy <- sapply(tau_g, function(u) bf_noisy(u)[2]) bf_truth    <- betfun(t(coef(fit_naive)), tau) slope_truth <- sapply(tau_g, function(u) bf_truth(u)[2])  plot(   tau_g, slope_me,   type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "steelblue",   ylim = range(slope_me, slope_noisy, slope_truth),   xlab = expression(tau), ylab = "Slope on X",   main = "Slope coefficient: ME-corrected vs naive vs truth" ) lines(tau_g, slope_noisy, col = "firebrick", lwd = 2, lty = 2) lines(tau_g, slope_truth, col = "black",     lwd = 1, lty = 3) legend("topleft",   legend = c("qrme (ME-corrected)", "Naive rq", "Infeasible truth"),   col    = c("steelblue", "firebrick", "black"),   lty    = c(1, 2, 3), lwd = c(2, 2, 1), bty = "n" )

title: Introduction to qrme: Quantile Regression with Measurement Error
text: qrme() provides straightforward interface -corrected quantile regression. workflow : Specify model formula choose tau. Choose distribution (n_mix, me_distribution). Tune MCMC (mcmc_draws, mcmc_burn_in, proposal_sd) EM (tol, max_em_iters) settings. Optionally add bootstrap SEs (se = TRUE). Use betfun() smooth coefficient curves AIC()/BIC() mixture-order selection. two-sided extension (outcome continuous treatment) see vignette("tsme-application").

title: Two-Sided Measurement Error: Intergenerational Income Mobility
text: vignette illustrates tsme(), two-sided measurement error estimator qrme package, using intergenerational income mobility application Callaway, Li, Murtazashvili, Tsyawo (2026). key idea outcome (child income) continuous treatment (father’s income) measured error, standard quantile regression estimates conditional distribution child income given father’s income biased. tsme() corrects bias : Running qrme() separately child income father income equations recover -corrected conditional quantile functions. Linking two via copula recover joint distribution latent (true) child father incomes. Deriving mobility statistics corrected joint distribution.

title: Two-Sided Measurement Error: Intergenerational Income Mobility
text: call reproduces main specification paper: Frank copula, Laplace measurement error distribution, one mixture component equation. Age controls enter child income father income equations. call takes roughly 90 minutes 10 cores. remainder vignette load pre-computed result bundled package:
code: tau     <- seq(0.02, 0.98, length.out = 25) t_values <- quantile(nlsy97$lpi, probs = seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.1))  set.seed(51526) fit <- tsme(   data            = nlsy97,   y_formula       = lci ~ ageC_97 + ageF,   t_formula       = lpi ~ ageC_97 + ageF,   tau             = tau,   t_values        = t_values,   y_n_mix         = 1L,   t_n_mix         = 1L,   copula          = "frank",   me_distribution = "laplace",   conv_patience   = 1L,   n_copula_me_draws = 1000L,   mcmc_draws      = 400L,   mcmc_burn_in    = 20L,   conv_criterion  = "params",   tol             = 1e-2,   max_em_iters    = 100L,   se              = TRUE,   n_boot          = 200L,   n_cores         = 10L,   boot_n_copula_me_draws = 500L,   boot_mcmc_draws = 200L,   boot_mcmc_burn_in = 10L,   boot_tol        = 5e-2,   verbose         = 2 ) fit <- nlsy97_tsme_fit

Distributional Effects Two-Sided Measurement Error: Application Intergenerational Income Mobility. arXiv:2107.09235 provides two main estimators: qrme() — Quantile regression measurement error outcome variable. EM-based implementation estimator developed Hausman, Liu, Luo, Palmer (2021, Econometrica), extended support finite Gaussian mixtures measurement error distribution. pseudo-EM algorithm alternates Metropolis–Hastings MCMC step (E-step) integrate latent outcome standard quantile regression M-step, iterating convergence. qrme() useful standalone tool setting dependent variable measured classical error. tsme() — Two-sided measurement error: joint quantile regression outcome continuous regressor measured error.
